key_insight: THReD’s user-confirmed LLM agent completed 92.7% of clinical-data preprocessing tasks on its first answer, but completion fell to 58.0% without a data profile.
clinical_relevance: Reliable, reproducible EHR preprocessing could support clinical AI research, although data-consolidation choices can materially change measured outcomes.
method: Benchmarked 141 tasks across seven categories over 2,550 agent episodes in four context configurations.
Tested preprocessing tools in six experiments using two real chronic-disease cohorts and large-scale synthetic data.
Evaluated reconstruction accuracy, dictionary mapping, pipeline reproducibility, subgroup differences and scaling.
evidence_signal: First-answer task completion was 92.7% (95% CI 88.1–96.4); dictionary mapping accuracy reached 99.0%, and all 2,176 pipeline replays produced byte-identical files under pinned dependencies.
watch_item: Agent testing used synthetic tables, so performance on heterogeneous real-world EHR workflows remains uncertain; same-day consolidation also shifted 90-day emergency revisit rates by up to 3.2 percentage points.
paper_title: Benchmark of THReD: Evaluating an LLM Agent and Its Preprocessing Tools for Turning Electronic Health Records into AI-Ready Datasets
